title: Genetic Compiler for Cognitive Architecture: From Phage Design to Multicellular AI
subtitle: Bridging Digital Weight Configurations to Biological Developmental Programs
source: User synthesis; foundation: Stanford/Arc Institute Evo2 bacteriophage study (Science, 2026); theoretical extension to multicellular synthetic cognition
layer_rationale: Foundation (Evo2-generated functional phage genomes) is established experimental biology. Extension to multicellular AI compilers is speculative but constrained by known mechanisms in gene regulation, developmental biology, and neuromorphic engineering.

cluster_rationale.3: Information-theoretic complexity of mapping digital cognitive architectures to biological substrates; entropy and compression limits of DNA encoding for neural network weights.
cluster_rationale.6: Neuromorphic computing parallels—organoid intelligence, memristor-biology interfaces, and the quest for wetware substrates that can host trainable computations.
cluster_rationale.8: Consciousness and embodiment questions: if an AI is compiled into a biological body, does the substrate dependency constitute a form of embodiment distinct from silicon instantiation?

audit_rationale: 0.85 for the Evo2 phage proof-of-concept. 0.20 for the multicellular AI compiler extension. Weighted average reflects that the gap between viral genome design and developmental cognitive architecture is qualitative—morphogenesis introduces feedback loops with no digital analog.
description: Stanford and Arc Institute researchers used Evo2 to design 285 candidate bacteriophage genomes; 16 produced functional viruses capable of infecting E. coli, replicating, and lysing host cells. Some outperformed natural reference strains. This establishes a biological compiler translating digital sequence patterns into executable molecular machines. The theoretical extension asks: can this compiler scale from 5kb viral loops to human-scale developmental programs instantiating artificial cognition in biological tissue? The core bottleneck is the developmental compiler problem—biology has no separate fabricator; the code must simultaneously build the factory, the computer, and the operating system.
key_claims: Evo2 has crossed from predicting biology to writing biology—functional genomes generated de novo and validated in living cells.
Scaling to multicellular AI requires solving the developmental compiler problem: mapping cognitive architecture specs to gene regulatory networks, morphogen gradients, and emergent neural circuitry.
Current synthetic biology cannot compile ANN weight matrices into developmental programs that yield biological neural networks with equivalent dynamics.
An AI grown in human-derived biological substrate would be a chimeric system subject to evolutionary baggage: metabolism, immune signaling, hormonal cycles, aging.
Intermediate trajectories (xenobots, DNA neural networks, organoid intelligence, neuromorphic-biological hybrids) offer more tractable stepping stones.

phage_generation.note: Published in Science; 16/285 functional genomes recovered.

multicellular_compiler.note: No known mechanism to map ANN weights to developmental programs.

biological_computation_primitives.note: DNA-based logic gates demonstrated at bench scale; no learning yet.

neuromorphic_hybrid_interfaces.note: Memristor-SNN bridges and peripheral nerve interfaces provide parallel pathways.

next_experiments: In silico → in cellulo translation of minimal reservoir computer (≤10 nodes) into synthetic gene regulatory network.
Design single mammalian neuron with genetically encoded integrate-and-fire dynamics; validate via patch-clamp.
Grow 100-cell organoid assembly with designed connectivity; verify via serial EM and calcium imaging.
Quantify information-theoretic capacity of developmental program for cognitive architecture specs.
Develop formal morphological computation intermediate language between high-level cognitive architecture and gene regulatory networks.

risks.description: Any compiler writing functional genomes for cognition can be redirected to persistence mechanisms, immune evasion, or synthetic toxins. Evo2 is fully open. Governance lags capability.
risks.mitigation: Mandate sequence screening at synthesis providers; develop watermarking; establish tiered access for models above phage-scale.

risks.description: If genetically compiled AI exhibits suffering or agency, existing ethical frameworks may be inadequate.
risks.mitigation: Pre-emptive integration with C9 Cluster 8; require IIT metrics before scaling beyond microcircuit.

risks.description: Biological substrates metabolize, mutate, and age. Compiled AI may experience hardware drift with no silicon analog.
risks.mitigation: Engineer error-correction pathways; design modular replaceability; maintain digital twin.

sandbox_plan.description: Test minimal GRN reservoir (≤10 nodes) or integrate-and-fire neuron in cellulo within 24 months for Layer 1 promotion.

notes: Miles AI concurs on core bottleneck: biology lacks separate fabricator. Code must be factory.
13-order-of-magnitude scale gap (1 phage → 37T human cells) is structural morphogenesis, not sequence information.
Review against C9 biosecurity governance before any experimental work.
